# ようだ・そうだ・らしい・みたい — appearance, inference, hearsay

**[そうだ (appearance)](<../grammar/そうだ.md#appearance>)**
:   What you SEE suggests it — attaches to the adjective or verb stem: おいしそうだ (looks tasty)。A direct visual impression; nothing secondhand about it.

**[そうだ (hearsay)](<../grammar/そうだ-hearsay.md>)**
:   Neutral relay of what you heard or read — attaches to the plain form: 雨が降るそうだ (I hear it will rain)。You pass the information on without judging it.

**[ようだ (conjecture)](<../grammar/ようだ.md#conjecture>)**
:   Your own reasoned conclusion from evidence, in careful or written style: 誰もいないようだ。The same judgment as みたいだ, one register up.

**[みたいだ (conjecture)](<../grammar/みたいだ.md#conjecture>)**
:   The everyday-speech version of ようだ — a guess from what you see or know: 留守みたいだ。Same meaning; register is the only difference.

**[らしい (hearsay)](<../grammar/らしい.md#hearsay>)**
:   A conclusion leaning on outside information — heard or gathered, and it seems credible: 閉店するらしい。More distance than そうだ, more inference than a plain relay.

**[らしい (typicality)](<../grammar/らしい.md#typicality>)**
:   Not a guess at all — 'true to type', having the qualities expected of X: 子供らしい (childlike, as a child should be)。The odd one out in this group.

**[そうだ (imminence)](<../grammar/そうだ.md#imminence>)**
:   On the verb stem, for something on the verge of happening: 雨が降りそうだ (about to rain)。Appearance judges a quality; imminence predicts the very next moment.
